page.note: The instrument ground, and the ground a metric tile sits back down onto.

panel.note: Any raised surface. One black, where four near-identical ones had accumulated.

line.note: Every rule and border on the dark ground, plus the scrollbar thumb. Warm, so it does not read as blue-cast grey-on-grey.

ink.note: Headings, figures, anything being read closely.

read.note: Body paragraphs. Bright enough to actually read on a near-black ground, which the greys it replaced were not.

quiet.note: The smallest print: disclaimers, placeholders, units, eyebrows. The floor, at 5.03:1 on the page and 4.82:1 on a panel. Absorbed a second grey 0.9:1 away.

accent.note: The mark, rules, fills, the selected ticker chip, the scrollbar thumb on hover, text selection at 55%. 2.16:1 on the page: NEVER text.

accent-text.note: The oxblood where it carries words, plus the caret and the keyboard focus outline. 5.08:1 on the page, 4.87:1 on a panel. Hue held at 3 degrees, saturation lifted 51% to 56% so it does not go dusty pink.

positive.note: One green, for a live state or a positive. Four emerald shades had been in use; the tone of a gain should not depend on which screen it is on.

positive-line.note: The border of a positive pill or a positive fill.

positive-fill.note: The ground of a positive pill.

amber.note: A warning that is a fact rather than a judgement: a data constraint, a basis the filing will not support.

paper.note: The reading ground: Margin Notes and the explainers under /learn/.

paper-ink.note: Headings and close reading on paper.

paper-quiet.note: The smallest print on paper. Fails the floor on the dark ground, which is why the two ramps are separate.

paper-accent-text.note: The darker cut of the oxblood that carries words on paper: 5.77:1. Paper also permits the deep accent as text; the dark ground does not.

title.purpose: The one heading that names a page. Newsreader 600 — a screen face with a newspaper cut, which is the register a company's accounts should arrive in.

section.purpose: A heading inside a page. Newsreader 600 at 20px.

body.purpose: Paragraphs, table rows and controls. Source Sans 3 at 15px.

small.purpose: Captions, labels and secondary lines. Source Sans 3 at 13px, which is the floor — there is no exemption below it anywhere, including the top bar.

figure.purpose: Not a step and not a face: the .font-figure class, which sets tabular and lining numerals on the body face. Alignment is a font feature rather than a font, so a column of numbers lines up without the prose beside it turning into a terminal dump.

label.purpose: The small step at weight 500, sentence case, normal tracking, never the accent colour. A label is a word and is set like one.

motion.name: disclose
motion.purpose: A Disclose body opening and closing. The chevron rotates 90deg over the same 200ms rather than swapping glyph, so the control does not reflow.

motion.name: condensed-header
motion.purpose: The condensed header entering once the full one has scrolled out.

motion.name: tile-stagger
motion.value: staggerChildren 50ms; child opacity 0 to 1, y 8px to 0

motion.name: colour-only-states
motion.purpose: Every hover and active state is a colour change. No lift, no scale, no shadow.

motion.name: marquee
motion.value: translateX(0) to translateX(-100%), 110s linear infinite, paused on hover
motion.purpose: The headline ticker. Starts at zero so the first headline is readable immediately.

motion.name: build-progress
motion.purpose: The BuildPipeline progress rule filling. Capped at 92% on purpose: the stage walk takes 4.5s and then holds while the fetch is still outstanding, and a bar sitting at 100% for ten seconds says the thing is done and broken. It never claims to be complete.

motion.name: build-card-enter
motion.value: opacity 0 to 1, y 12px to 0, scale 0.98 to 1, 300ms ease-out
motion.purpose: The BuildPipeline overlay card entering over the page colour at 85% with a small backdrop blur.

motion.name: note-rotate
motion.value: crossfade opacity 0 to 1 with y 6px, 350ms ease-out; one note holds 6500ms
motion.purpose: The did-you-know note replacing itself inside the loading card. Under prefers-reduced-motion the note still changes, it simply does not move: movement is suppressed, information is not.

breakpoints.name: prose-ragged
breakpoints.purpose: At or below this width prose stops justifying and goes ragged-right; justifying a narrow column forces gaps into every line.

verification.what: Compares src/design/tokens.ts against the :root block of src/index.css and fails if any --m-* disagrees; measures every token in TEXT_ON_DARK and TEXT_ON_PAPER against 4.5:1 on every ground; asserts accent stays out of the dark-ground text list; fails a component that declares a palette hex of its own.

components.description: The one figure a screen exists to show: an eyebrow above, the number large, monospaced and alone, an optional pill on its baseline. A FIGURE IS ALWAYS INK and there is no prop to make it otherwise — the tone prop was removed rather than left unused. The oxblood is reserved for the mark and for a signal that is meant: the premium badge beside the figure, where being red is the point.

components.name: Disclose Row
components.description: Where the prose went, and now the shape four screens are built out of. A real button with aria-expanded over a controlled region; the chevron rotates rather than swapping glyph so the control cannot reflow. A measurement may stay visible on the closed row — a trailing phrase, a figure, or a Pill carrying the effect. The body is capped at 68ch HERE, on the disclosure, not on the paragraph inside it. A dense variant drops the top rule and halves the padding, for a disclosure nested inside another or sitting under a question.
components.html: The perpetuity method grows the last forecast year for ever at the terminal rate; the exit multiple capitalises that year’s EBITDA at an assumed multiple. They are never averaged, because an average is neither method’s answer.

components.notes: The 68ch cap is literal and must not be "simplified" to max-w-prose: src/index.css redefines .max-w-prose as max-width: none; text-align: justify, so that class WIDENS a column here. max-w-prose may still be written on a paragraph inside a disclosure, where it means only "justify this". The trailing slot goes full-width under the summary below 640px and to the far end of the row above it; left as one flex line it became two cramped columns of wrapped text at 414px.

components.name: Constraint Row
components.description: One data constraint as one Disclose row, with a Pill in the trailing slot carrying the largest effect it could have on the value per share. Pill tone encodes severity and nothing else: negative is a refusal (no value shown), warn is a warning (flagged above the model), neutral is a note (listed only). Every entry used to be expanded at once — a label, two size tags, a detail paragraph, an effect paragraph and a source line, in a filled box, for each of up to a dozen constraints — which could not answer the reader’s actual question ("how many, and does any of them matter to the number I am looking at"), because answering it meant reading all of it. The account of a constraint now opens on the row it belongs to.

components.name: Build Pipeline Overlay
components.description: The loading state, as a centred overlay on the page colour at 85% with a small backdrop blur. The five-row labelled checklist is ONE capped progress rule: a 1px hairline rail with an oxblood fill, the count on the right, the current stage named beneath it in the quietest type on the card. A reader cannot act on "Discounting cash flows" and only needs to know the thing is alive and roughly how far along; the stage names stay because the argument of this site is that the workings are visible. THE CONTENT IS ONE MYTH-VERSUS-FACT CARD and the progress is the furniture: the label "Common myth" in the quiet eyebrow, the belief in italic body, the correction set like the headline it is in the Newsreader display face, and the mechanism behind a ⓘ rather than printed under it. NOTHING APPEARS FOR THE FIRST SECOND, so a build that finishes inside it closes with the progress rule alone rather than flashing a sentence nobody could read. The belief is shown alone for 2.2s before the correction joins it, the two beats are scheduled once, and the card may be replaced only while its myth is still alone — a correction rescheduled late is one the reader never sees, because the overlay closes as soon as the work is done. The card announces its own progress through aria-live="polite"; the card itself is aria-live="off" deliberately, because a card changing underneath would talk over it.

components.notes: The shipped card carries a Tailwind shadow-2xl in src/components/motionPrimitives.tsx. It is NOT reproduced here and is not a system rule: this system declares no shadows and conveys depth tonally plus hairline. The fact’s clamp(1.25rem, 2.4vw, 1.75rem) is what the component draws and is recorded as a component literal, not promoted to a type token; it is not a declared step on the DESIGN.md ramp. The foot line is sentence case, like every label on the site since the one-pairing pass: tracked capitals at 13px ran to three shouting lines on a phone, for the least important sentence on the card.

components.name: Section Tab Bar
components.description: One tab per section of a company, each at its own address. The panel ground inside the same hairline box as the identity block above it; hairlines drawn BY the tabs, never by a line-coloured ground showing through a gap, which puts a slab of line colour past the last tab. The current tab takes the page ground and a two-pixel oxblood underline as an inset shadow, so it reads as cut out of the bar. Scrolls horizontally on a phone rather than wrapping or collapsing to a menu.
components.html: <nav class="ds-tabs" aria-label="Company sections"><button type="button" class="ds-tab ds-tab-current" aria-current="page">Overview</button><button type="button" class="ds-tab">Financials</button><button type="button" class="ds-tab">Filings</button><button type="button" class="ds-tab">Model</button></nav>
components.css: .ds-tabs { display: flex; overflow-x: auto; background: var(--m-panel, #111114); border-left: 1px solid var(--m-line, #262521); border-right: 1px solid var(--m-line, #262521); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--m-line, #262521); } .ds-tab { flex: none; font-family: var(--font-figure); font-size: 13px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--m-muted, #A8A29A); background: transparent; border: 0; border-right: 1px solid var(--m-line, #262521); padding: 12px 16px; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: color 0.2s, background 0.2s; } .ds-tab:hover { color: var(--m-ink, #F2F0EA); background: rgba(11,11,13,0.4); } .ds-tab-current { color: var(--m-ink, #F2F0EA); background: var(--m-page, #0B0B0D); box-shadow: inset 0 -2px 0 var(--m-accent, #8B1E1E); }
components.notes: A tab that is not built renders a heading, a neutral "being built" pill and one sentence naming what it will carry. Never a greyed table or placeholder rows.

components.name: Two-Axis Price Chart
components.description: Plain SVG, no charting library, because a library decides for itself what to do with a gap and this chart must never join a line across a ratio that does not exist. The price is a 1.5px ink line on a fill fading from 10% ink; it owns the LEFT axis. An overlay is amber and owns the RIGHT axis, always — never one shared scale, which flattens one quantity into the baseline. A second overlay line is dashed in read oxblood on its own scale, with the caption saying which axis belongs to which. Where the series has no point the path breaks rather than bridging.
components.html: 262 daily closes. Point at the chart to read a day.
components.css: .ds-chart { background: var(--m-panel, #111114); border: 1px solid var(--m-line, #262521); padding: 20px; } .ds-chart-fill { fill: rgba(242,240,234,0.10); } .ds-chart-price { fill: none; stroke: var(--m-ink, #F2F0EA); stroke-width: 1.5; stroke-linejoin: round; } .ds-chart-overlay { fill: none; stroke: var(--m-amber, #C79A2E); stroke-width: 1.25; stroke-linejoin: round; } .ds-chart-overlay-second { stroke: var(--m-accent-text, #D05E58); stroke-dasharray: 4 3; } .ds-chart-axis { font-family: var(--font-figure); font-size: 11px; fill: var(--m-quiet, #85816F); } .ds-chart-axis-right { fill: var(--m-amber, #C79A2E); } .ds-chart-readout { font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 13px; color: var(--m-quiet, #85816F); margin: 8px 0 0; min-height: 22px; }
components.notes: The readout sits in a fixed place under the chart, never following the pointer: a tooltip that moves makes the eye chase it, and its figures are meant to be compared with the ones above. The break in the overlay path above is deliberate — it is what a gap looks like.

narrative.overview:
Marginalia is a warm near-black instrument with a paper annex. Everything on the instrument side is measured in a single warm ramp — a warm page, a warm off-white ink, and warm greys between them — because the one cool grey the build used to carry (Tailwind's zinc, 62 uses sitting beside 300 uses of a warm grey) read as faintly dirty against the ground and nobody could say why. The reading side — Margin Notes and the explainers under /learn/ — is a separate ramp on paper, not the same ramp inverted, because a colour legible on one ground is usually not legible on the other.

Density is a value here, not a side effect. An eyebrow label, a figure at 17px, a hairline and no shadow: a professional reads a row of tiles at a glance and wants them close together, and the airy version of the same card says "dashboard" rather than "terminal". The governing pattern of the shipped company screen is the number first, the explanation on demand. A figure is large, monospaced and alone; everything that accounts for it sits behind a disclosure that opens beside the figure rather than in a footnote at the bottom of the panel. The prose was never the fault — it is the reason to trust the number — but a reader who already trusts it should not walk past three sentences to find the value.

Contrast is a property of the token, not of the component. Every colour that carries words clears 4.5:1 on every ground it is used on; verify/scenarios.mts measures it and npm run verify fails the run if a token drops below. The one deliberate exception is stated as its own token rather than remembered: the oxblood that carries words is a different value from the oxblood that is a square.
keyCharacteristics: Two grounds, two ramps: a warm near-black instrument, warm paper for reading.
Hairlines and tonal layering only. Not one box-shadow in the build.
Square corners. Radius appears only as a full circle, on a status dot or a diagram ring.
Every figure tabular; every title Newsreader at 600, cut tight. One pairing, four sizes.
One red, one green, one amber. Their rarity is what makes them mean anything.
A red square, not a full stop, ends a heading.
Even the surfaces nobody draws — scrollbar, selection, caret, focus ring — come from the palette.

rules.name: The Mark Is Not Text Rule
rules.body: accent is the mark, the rule and the fill, and is never set as type at any size. Words in oxblood take accent-text. The two are separate tokens so the distinction is stated rather than remembered, and the contrast check asserts accent stays out of the text list.

rules.name: The Two Grounds Rule
rules.body: Dark tokens are for instrument screens, paper tokens for reading screens. Never carry a token across grounds, and never derive one ramp from the other by inversion.

rules.name: The 4.5:1 Floor Rule
rules.body: Any token that carries words clears 4.5:1 on every ground it appears on. A colour is chosen by measurement, not by eye, and the measurement is enforced by npm run verify.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: One red, one green, one amber. A new state borrows an existing tone or goes grey; it does not introduce a hue.

rules.name: The Palette Lives In One File Rule
rules.body: src/design/tokens.ts is the source; src/index.css mirrors it as --m-* custom properties and @theme names them as --color-* utilities pointing at those properties, so there is no third copy to drift. A component that declares a palette hex of its own fails verification.

rules.name: The No Browser Default Rule
rules.body: The scrollbar, the selection, the caret and the focus ring are palette colours. A default blue selection is the one colour on the page that belongs to no palette, and it is the difference between a page that was built and one that was assembled.

rules.name: The Density Rule
rules.body: Rows of measures sit close. If a surface feels airy it is reading as a dashboard rather than a terminal, and the padding is wrong.

rules.name: The Blocks Line Up Rule
rules.body: A paragraph, a table and a chart in the same panel share one left and one right edge. Three different prose widths beside full-width tables is what makes a page read as ragged columns floating in empty space.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Separation is a 1px warm line or a one-step tonal change. A surface is never lifted off the page with a shadow, a glow or a gradient.

rules.name: The Zero Advance Width Rule
rules.body: marginRight: -0.21em on the mark is not a tuning value and is never adjusted. Render the mark through the one Mark component; never hand-roll the square, and never write a literal full stop before one.

rules.name: The Figure Is Always Ink Rule
rules.body: A figure is set in ink, at every scale, and there is no option to make it otherwise. The tone prop was removed from Figure rather than left unused, because an option to make a figure red is an invitation to. The intrinsic value was set in oxblood at first and read as a warning rather than as the headline it is: on a dark instrument screen a red number is the one that has gone wrong. The red belongs to the mark and to a signal that is meant — the premium badge beside the figure, where being red is the point.

rules.name: The 68ch Measure Rule
rules.body: A Disclose body is capped at 68ch on the disclosure itself, and that literal must not be "simplified" to max-w-prose. On this site max-w-prose does the opposite of what its name says: src/index.css sets .max-w-prose { max-width: none; text-align: justify } as a deliberate house rule, so writing it WIDENS the column and justifies it. A disclosure opens inside a full-width panel, so without a cap its prose ran past 140 characters a line; 68ch is inside the 65-75 a line should hold. max-w-prose may still be written on a paragraph inside, where it means only "justify this", which is all it has ever meant here.

rules.name: The Severity Is The Tone Rule
rules.body: On a constraint row the Pill tone carries severity and nothing else: negative is a refusal (no value is shown), warn is a warning (flagged above the model as well), neutral is a note (listed only). The badge states the largest effect the missing figure could have on the value per share, so the row answers "does this matter to the number I am looking at" without being opened.

rules.name: The One Pairing Rule
rules.body: Newsreader for titles, Source Sans 3 for everything else including every number. A screen that wants a third voice uses weight, colour or size from the four steps. There is no editorial face, no label face and no code face.

rules.name: The Figures Are Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number is set with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums lining-nums, carried by .font-figure. This replaces The Figures Are Mono Rule: the purpose was always alignment, and alignment is a font feature rather than a font.

rules.name: The Uniform Label Rule
rules.body: A label is sentence case, at the small step, at weight 500, with normal letter-spacing. No uppercase and no tracking. Switched off at the source in index.css and in the EYEBROW and LABEL constants, so a screen that still writes uppercase gets sentence case.

rules.name: The No Red Labels Rule
rules.body: The accent never carries a label. An eyebrow keeps its oxblood hairline and the words themselves are muted. Oxblood as text survives only where it is a signal that is meant: a link, a changed figure, a refusal.

rules.name: The 13px Floor Rule
rules.body: Nothing is set below 13px, and there are no exemptions. The top bar needed one while its labels were spaced capitals; sentence case is narrower and the same seven labels fit at the small step.

rules.name: The Prose Is Not A Table Rule
rules.body: What distinguishes a column of figures from a sentence is the tabular setting, not the family. Both are Source Sans 3, so a summary, a basis sentence and a figure sit in one row without the row changing its mind about itself.

rules.name: The Families Live In The Tokens Rule
rules.body: tokens.ts exports TYPE and SIZE; index.css mirrors them as --font-* and --m-size-*; every rule and component reads those. No component and no stylesheet rule names a font family literally.

rules.name: The Four Steps Rule
rules.body: Title, section, body, small, and nothing between them. The site asked for twenty-five sizes between 9px and 62px before this; the remapping block in index.css snaps any stray arbitrary size onto one of the four, so a twenty-sixth cannot be introduced by writing one.

rules.name: The Empty End Rule
rules.body: Hairlines between tabs are drawn by the tabs themselves, never by letting a line-coloured ground show through a gap. Drawn the second way, the space past the last tab is a slab of line colour across the page, which reads as a broken element rather than a divider.

rules.name: The Two-Axis Rule
rules.body: On a chart, the price owns the left axis and an overlay owns the right, in amber, always. Never one shared scale: a price-to-earnings of 46 and a price of $344 share an axis only by flattening one of them into the baseline, and a flat line is a claim about a quantity that did not move. Two overlay lines each get their own scale, the second dashed, with the caption saying which axis is which.

rules.name: The Gap Is A Gap Rule
rules.body: Where a series has no point — a loss year with no price-to-earnings, a day before the earliest filing held — the path breaks and starts again rather than bridging, and the readout says why in words. Interpolating invents a figure and a flat join invents a period that did not move.

rules.name: The Unbuilt Section Rule
rules.body: A section that is not built shows a heading, a neutral "being built" pill and one sentence naming what it will carry. Never a greyed-out table, placeholder rows or an empty state dressed as real data: a mocked-up section is the most convincing false claim a site can make.

rules.name: The Common Myth Rule
rules.body: A myth-versus-fact card is labelled "Common myth" — eyebrow, sentence case, 13px, quiet — and nothing on the screen, with the mechanism open or closed, says "this company". The cards are about how accounts behave; the same sentence introduced as a finding about the company on screen is a verdict on a security. The sentence behind the ⓘ still gives the condition that picked the card, because the reader is owed it, and still puts it as education.

rules.name: The No Flicker Rule
rules.body: A screen does not show something it is about to take away. The loading card waits a second before it appears, because a cached answer returns in a few hundred milliseconds and a sentence that appears and goes inside that is a flicker rather than a sentence. A build that finishes inside the second closes with the progress rule as its only content, which is honest: there was nothing to wait through.

rules.name: The Two Beats Rule
rules.body: The belief first, alone; the correction a beat later. A fact printed under the belief at the same instant is a caption on it, and a reader has to have had the chance to agree with the myth for the correction to land. The beats are scheduled once and the card may be replaced only while its myth is still alone: restarting them when better data arrives loses the fact, because the screen closes as soon as the work is done, and a belief shown without its correction is worse than showing nothing.

rules.name: A Tooltip Is Not A Title
rules.body: The ⓘ panel is prose — sans, weight 400, upright, 13px — whatever it hangs off. Letting it inherit was invisible while every ⓘ sat on a sans table row, and produced three lines of Newsreader medium the first time one was put at the end of a sentence set in the display face.

rules.name: The Editable Row Rule
rules.body: A figure that looks editable must change the answer on the same screen, and the screen must show what the answer was. An input that moves a number beside it and not the valuation under it invites a reader to test an assumption and then lies about the result. A list of such inputs is text with a dashed quiet underline, not a column of bordered boxes: nine boxes reads as a form waiting to be filled in, and this is a statement of what the model used with corrections available.

dos: Do take colour from the ramp by utility name (text-ink, bg-panel, border-line, text-accent-text), which resolves through --m- to src/design/tokens.ts.
Do set every number with .font-figure, which carries tabular-nums and lining-nums, including any number that tweens.
Do use accent-text for oxblood words and accent for the mark, rules and fills.
Do separate with a 1px warm hairline or a one-step tonal change.
Do keep square corners (0px) on panels, tiles, chips, pills and buttons.
Do put the figure first and fold its account into a Disclose beside it, leaving a measurement visible on the closed row where a reader needs it.
Do render the heading mark through the Mark component, keeping marginRight: -0.21em.
Do build new screens from the instrument.tsx primitives (Figure, Pill, MetricTile, Disclose, RefStrip) rather than new markup.
Do give an interactive row a real <button> with aria-expanded and a palette :focus-visible outline.
Do run npm run verify after touching a colour: it compares tokens.ts against index.css and measures every text token against the 4.5:1 floor.
Do keep prose at full panel width, justified with hyphenation above 640px.
donts: Don't set accent (#8B1E1E) as text at any size. It is 2.16:1 on the page.
Don't declare a palette hex inside a component; verification fails it.
Don't add a second green, a second red, a second panel black, or a cool grey. The ground is warm, and a cool grey on it reads as faintly dirty.
Don't name a font family in a component or a stylesheet rule. Families come from TYPE in src/design/tokens.ts and nowhere else.
Don't add a box-shadow, a glow or a gradient to lift a surface.
Don't set type below 13px. There is no exemption any more, including the top bar.
Don't add a font size between the four steps; the remapping block in index.css will snap it onto one of them anyway.
Don't set a label in capitals, track it out, or colour it with the accent.
Don't leave a browser default on the scrollbar, the selection, the caret or the focus ring.
Don't loosen tile or row padding into an airy grid; density is the register.
Don't round, rename or re-derive a token hex. The frontmatter values are the measured ones.
